description:
PearList keeps your household's shared lists in sync across everyone's phones, with no account, no server and no company in the middle.

Make a grocery list, a to-do list or a chore board. Anyone in your household can add items, check them off, rename them, assign them and delete them, and every change syncs directly between your phones. Assign an item to a person and any list doubles as a shared chore board.

There is no sign-up and no login. You join a household by scanning a QR code or tapping an invite link. From then on everyone sees and edits the same lists.
  
Because PearList is peer-to-peer, your lists live only on your devices. They are never uploaded to a server, so no company can read them, sell them or lose them in a breach. Everything syncs encrypted, directly device to device.

Features
 - Multiple shared lists per household: groceries, to-dos, chores
 - Add, check, rename, assign and delete items, synced to everyone
 - Assign items to a person to use any list as a chore board
 - Join by QR code or invite link, no account needed
 - Works offline, syncs when your devices are online together
 - Open source and private by design: no account, no ads, no tracking

PearList is fully open source: https://github.com/peerloomllc/pearlist
promotionalText: Shared household lists that sync directly between your phones. No account, no server, no tracking. Groceries, to-dos and chores, private by design.
whatsNew:
## What's Changed

  ### Notes
  
  Lists are not the only thing a household needs to share. PearList now has notes: a plain, free-text page for the wifi password, a recipe, what the plumber said, anything that is not a tick-box.

  A note lives in your space like any other list, so everyone sees it and everyone can edit it. Two people typing in the same note at the same time is fine. Both sets of changes are kept, and neither person's text quietly disappears.

  ### Ask before deleting

  Renaming or deleting a list now happens behind a confirmation. Deleting is shared and permanent, so a stray tap should not wipe a note the whole house was using.

  ### Picks up where you left off

  Come back to PearList and it reopens the space and list you were last looking at, instead of dropping you at the overview every time.

  ### Fixes

  - Fixed a frozen screen when returning to PearList on GrapheneOS. The app looked stuck, taps did nothing visible, and only a restart cleared it.
  - Fixed note text going missing if you switched apps a moment after typing it.
